clue.text: Allegedly rude greeting from lout to flashily dressed man

parts.note: a yob is a loutish young man
lair is Australian slang for a man who dresses showily

explanation.surface: A thug shouts something coarse at a dandy in loud clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting is the one George W. Bush reportedly gave Tony Blair at the 2006 G8 summit, widely reported as disrespectful. LAIR is Australian slang, so it may be unfamiliar.
explanation.definitionFit: Bush's informal hail to the British prime minister, caught on an open microphone, was reported as a casual, rather rude salutation.

clue.text: Lament about maiden can go heavenward

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up toward heaven means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
may and can both express permission

explanation.surface: Someone mourns as a girl's tin container is launched skyward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go heavenward' suits a down light: the whole charade is read upward, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to whine or wail persistently, a complaining sort of lamentation.

clue.text: Listed as sick, unable to get up?

indicators.note: someone unable to get up is laid up in bed, so the word for sick is placed within the word for bed

parts.note: taken with the indicator phrase: being in bed is what the condition amounts to
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone is put on the sick list because they cannot rise from bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Being laid up 'unable to get up' means being in bed, so the setter leaves the container to be inferred rather than signalled by a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: Billed can mean announced or listed, as performers are billed on a programme.

clue.text: True — a ham is, sadly!

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of the preceding words are in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: A lament that a poor actor really is as bad as everyone says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges TRUE A HAM IS, and the whole clue doubles as a description of a ham actor's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an overacting performer, whose work is unprofessional and lacking in skill.

clue.text: In summary, harvest's about to be gathered in

indicators.note: gathered in means taken within, so the abbreviation goes inside the harvest word

parts.note: to reap is to harvest; the 's is just 'has' or a link
C, for circa, is a Latin abbreviation meaning about

explanation.surface: Briefly put, the harvest is about to be brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap is a brief summary of what has been said, so the phrase 'in summary' sums it up.

clue.text: To walk like a duck? Let's have no duck nonsense!

indicators.note: having no duck means the zero-shaped letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: waddle is the rocking walk of a duck
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: A remark on duck-like walking ends by dismissing duck jokes as silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' appears twice: first the bird, then the cricket score of nought that gives O. Removing that O from TO WADDLE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly, trivial talk, a direct synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Blunt upsetter stopped by one king, being upset

definitions.text: Blunt upsetter stopped by one king, being upset

indicators.note: upset suggests a knocked-over mixture, so the combined letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An outspoken troublemaker, checked by a monarch, is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry II reputedly cried 'Will no one rid me of this turbulent priest?' of Thomas Becket, the outspoken troublemaker later killed. 'stopped by' only says the one-king letters join the pool before 'being upset' shuffles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Becket, the outspoken archbishop who defied the king and was murdered after Henry's outburst, is the man so described.

clue.text: Someone murdered Lincoln, then left

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A reference to an assassinated president who then departed.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln was himself murdered, which makes the definition look like it describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abel was killed by his brother Cain, the first murder victim.

clue.text: Semicircular piece, excellent stuff from the butcher

parts.note: the capital letter D is shaped like a half circle
ripping is old British slang for splendid or excellent

explanation.surface: An arc-shaped cut of something fine bought at the meat counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dripping is the fat that runs from roasting meat, traditionally sold by butchers in Britain.

clue.text: Setting up of ballot in which the Right ousts the Left

indicators.note: ousts means replaces, so one letter takes the place of the other in the vote word

parts.note: an election is a vote decided by ballot
L is the abbreviation for left
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A political vote in which the right wing throws out the left.
explanation.definitionFit: An erection is the act of putting up or building something, such as a structure being set up.

clue.text: Country participating in formal talks

indicators.note: participating in signals the letters take part within the run of the next two words

explanation.surface: A nation takes part in official negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Monk is church's leader — a jolly choice

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
elite means select or choice

explanation.surface: A monk is the head of his church, a cheerful pick for the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective but is the slang noun for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmelites are friars of the Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, a religious order of monks.

clue.text: This additional exam

parts.note: this refers to the clue's own number, 11
plus means additional or extra

explanation.surface: A supplementary test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' points at the clue number: the clue is 11 across, so 'This' gives the number eleven. The exam was taken by British children of about eleven to decide grammar-school places.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleven-plus is a British selection examination sat at the end of primary school.

clue.text: Gentle rain where land goes out to sea

definitions.meaning: a few light drops of rain falling is said to be spitting

definitions.text: where land goes out to sea
definitions.meaning: a narrow point of land jutting into the water is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a light drizzle and a narrow tongue of land projecting into the sea.

clue.text: Front of toe enters shoe, one lacking external support?

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the toe's initial is placed within the footwear word

parts.note: a sandal is a type of open shoe

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as its spelt-out word

explanation.surface: A toe pokes into a shoe, and someone stands with nothing to lean on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stand-alone works independently, without being propped up by anything else.

clue.text: Slowing down later on land ploughed up

indicators.note: ploughed up land is turned over and broken, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer will get to tilling the field afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallentando is a musical direction meaning gradually getting slower.

clue.text: Face up to crazy ideas being rejected

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of the next word are in disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is told to confront the fact that their mad notions are being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DIAL into LAID; 'crazy' rearranges IDEAS into ASIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid aside has been put away and set apart, that is, dismissed or discarded.

clue.text: Meat cutter grabbed by brother?

indicators.note: grabbed by means held inside, so the cutter word sits within the sibling word

parts.note: sib, short for sibling, can mean a brother
a parer is a knife or tool for cutting away peel

explanation.surface: A sibling seizes the carving knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare rib is a cut of pork from the ribs with most of the meat trimmed off.

clue.text: Powerful politician before (say) Brown's time

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
Gordon Brown is Scottish, so '(say)' marks him as an example of a Scot

explanation.surface: An influential politician who served ahead of Gordon Brown's tenure.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott was Labour's deputy prime minister under Tony Blair. Gordon Brown is the Scottish Labour prime minister who followed Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: As deputy prime minister for a decade, he was one of the most senior figures in government.

clue.text: Odd pair : England goalkeeper and American socialite

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of place, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: Peter Shilton holds the record for most caps as England goalkeeper

explanation.surface: An unlikely couple: an English football keeper and a US celebrity heiress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges PAIR into PARI. Shilton was England's goalkeeper from 1970 to 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hilton hotel heiress became famous as a celebrity socialite in the 2000s.

clue.text: Shot that may have some lead in it

definitions.meaning: a cricket stroke deflecting the ball off the bat's face

definitions.text: that may have some lead in it
definitions.meaning: ... is an old mining term for a lustrous ore, as in lead ..., the mineral galena

explanation.walkthrough: Lead glance is galena, the chief ore of lead; the clue sounds like it is about a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a deflecting cricket stroke and a shiny metallic ore such as galena.

clue.text: See 5
Dean goes through Brecon

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, the thing that flows through the town
the River Usk flows through Brecon in Wales

explanation.surface: A cathedral official travels via a Welsh market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean Rusk was US Secretary of State in the 1960s. Brecon is a Welsh town on the River Usk.
explanation.definitionFit: Dean is the first name of the American statesman Dean Rusk, so the name points to his surname.

clue.text: Waterfall's fantastic — he waxed lyrical

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly imaginative, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses about a marvellous cascade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waxed' means made gramophone records: the American jazz pianist recorded many witty songs.
explanation.definitionFit: The jazz pianist and songwriter cut many records of lively songs, so he literally put lyrics on wax.

clue.text: To walk without energy is difficult

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the walking word wraps the energy symbol

parts.note: to step is to walk
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Walking with no strength left is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep slope or demand is hard to manage, so the word can mean difficult.

clue.text: Driver of good-looking model

definitions.meaning: Stirling ... was a celebrated British racing driver
Kate ... is a famous English fashion model

explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to racing driver Stirling Moss and to supermodel Kate Moss.

clue.text: Mineral supplying the iron dose half contaminated

indicators.note: contaminated means corrupted, so the letters are mixed up
half of the four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A mineral that supplies the iron in a partly tainted dose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes DO from DOSE; 'contaminated' rearranges THE IRON plus DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodonite is a pink manganese silicate mineral used as an ornamental stone.

clue.text: In spring there's loss of black cat

indicators.note: loss of means taking away, so the letter is removed from the spring word

parts.note: bounce means spring or springiness
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: In springtime a black cat goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but means bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asian mountains.

clue.text: Fabric in a coil wife removed to be put outside

indicators.note: put outside means placed around, so the two-letter word wraps the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: removed means the letter is taken out of the coil word

parts.note: a twist is a coil or turn

explanation.surface: Cloth wrapped in a spiral, with the wife taken away to be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put outside' looks like an instruction to eject something; it actually means the little verb wraps around everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Batiste is a fine, light cotton or linen fabric.

clue.text: Chief officer flawless? Twisted inside

indicators.note: twisted inside means the inner pair of letters of the flawless word is turned round

parts.note: perfect means flawless

explanation.surface: Is the head officer without fault? He is warped within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted inside' turns the ER in PERFECT around to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefect is a senior official, such as a chief administrator in French or Roman government.
